newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Flughafen Wien '96 group net down 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Flughafen Wien '96 group net down 11 pct.

text.p: Vienna airport operator Flughafen Wien AG said on Thursday 1996 net profit eased 11 percent to 602 million schillings ($49.5 million), blaming the fall on "incentive payments" it made to its airline customers.
Pretax earnings fell to 885 million schillings, from 961.4 million a year earlier, the group said in a statement released ahead of its annual earnings news conference.
Flughafen attributed the decline in profits to a set of measures it had to take to "secure its long-term earnings potential."

"These are incentives to all airline customers, and particularly our most important customers, which are interested in the development of Vienna as an international hub, to tie them to Vienna International Airport for the long term," it said without providing further details.
Despite the fall in earnings, Flughafen said it would raise its dividend to 16 schillings per share from 12 schillings in 1995.
The Association of Austrian Analysts on Wednesday said earnings per share had eased to 29 schillings from 33 schillings per share a year ago.
Flughafen declined to give an earnings outlook for the current year, but said it expected to reach its goal of "almost" 10 million passengers this year.
Last year, passenger volume rose seven percent to 9.14 million, while freight traffic rose 3.2 percent to 130,000 tons. A total of 60 airlines is currently operating from Vienna airport.

Flughafen's shares, which on Wednesday closed at 518.50 schillings, were suspended on the Vienna stock exchange on Thursday morning and were expected to resume trading at 0900 GMT. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 12.16 Austrian Schillings)
